messages.subject: Experimental Shiny callback mechanism
parts:
I was hoping that R can have some simple callback mechanism or non-blocking I/O like Javascript. Then I stumbled upon svSocket which can set up a non-blocking socket server. So I combined it with the parallel package and created an experimental non-blocking callback mechanism for Shiny.

Please let me know if there's a easier or better way to do this! Or if Shiny already supports something like this natively!

My program architecture is quite simple: I have a list called call.back.register which can be added to and stores the callback function and the non-blocking socket server information. Then I use the go.socket function from my gosocket package to create a separate process to run a non-blocking socket server. When the go.socket is run I also update the call.back.register with the go.socket information and a callback function. 

There is a reactiveTimer being observed to periodically check if a certain temporary file exists, that temp file will be created by the separate process when it has finished processing. In this case the 'processing' was to sleep for 30 seconds, but you can replace it with any other heavy duty stuff (perfect for non-blocking I/O). Hence I have constructed the skeleton of a non-blocking I/O system with callbacks in Shiny!


Install
install.packages(c("devtools","svSocket")) # if not already installed
devtools::install_github("gosocket","analytixware")
devtools::install_github("shinysky","analytixware") # if not already installed

Run Gist
shiny::runGist("7991982")

ui.R
library(shiny)
library(shinysky)

# Define UI for application that plots random distributions 
shinyUI(basicPage(
     actionButton("btn","Click me to run callback",style.class="danger")     
     ,shinyalert("alert1")
     ,shinyalert("alert2")
     ,sliderInput("obs", 
                 "Number of observations:", 
                 min = 1,
                 max = 1000, 
                 value = 500)
    ,plotOutput("distPlot")
        
  )
)

server.R

library(shiny)
library(shinysky)
library(gosocket)

# Define server logic required to generate and plot a random distribution
shinyServer(function(input, output,session) {
  
  call.back.register <- list(go.sockets = list(),call.back.func = list())
  
  a <- reactiveTimer(session=session)
  
  # a reactive timer to watch the call.back.register
  observe({
    a() 
    #print("periodic checking if file exsits")
    
    if(length(call.back.register$go.sockets) == 1) {
      #browser()
      gs <- call.back.register$go.sockets[[1]]
      if(file.exists(gs$tmp.f)) {
       # browser()
          call.back.register$go.sockets[[1]] <<- NULL      
          f <- call.back.register$call.back.func[[1]]
          call.back.register$call.back.func[[1]] <<- NULL
          f()        
          showshinyalert("alert2","The callback has been called!",session,"success")
        }
      }
  })
  
  
  # add a callback when the button is clicked
  observe({
    if(input$btn  == 0) return()
    
    tmp.f <- gsub("\\","/",tempfile(),fixed=TRUE)
    code <- sprintf("write(1,file='%s')",tmp.f)
    gs <- go.socket(sprintf("Sys.sleep(30);%s",code))
    #gs <- go.socket(sprintf("%s",code))
    gs$tmp.f <- tmp.f
    
    
    showshinyalert("alert1","It is sleeping for 30 seconds in another process! But this is not blocked! When it wakes up it will trigger another alert",session,"success")
    l <- length(call.back.register$go.sockets) + 1        
    call.back.register$go.sockets[l] <<- list(gs)
    call.back.register$call.back.func[l] <<- list(f = function() {print("call back successful")})
  })
  
  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({    
    # generate an rnorm distribution and plot it
    dist <- rnorm(input$obs)
    hist(dist)
  })
})

messages.author: 10be2e2b09c8c598
messages.subject: Re: Experimental Shiny callback mechanism
parts:
I can imagine that the solution is not easy or straightforward.  While broadly interested in the topic, I am currently most interested in how this functionality could improve geospatial workflows for https://www.r-consortium.org/blog/2016/08/22/the-r-consortium-funds-three-projects-in-july.  Accessing R natively through the console while also maintaining a bi-directional communication between an interactive view and R would be very helpful.  Another option that I considered would be for local embedded Shiny an eval console in the browser that allows the user full access to R maybe through Ace or codemirror.  I understand this is a security nightmare for non-local Shiny, but it seems as dangerous as a R console for individual consumption.  I am not sure if this option is easier or harder.  Seeing the output from the command might be difficult, but I guess printing in the R console would be ok or just filling a <pre> in browser would also be ok.

Kent

My use case for non-blocking shiny bits would involve allowing the
user to punch a button that triggers the shiny app to submit a job to
a compute cluster then let the user keep interacting with the app.

Once the job would finish, you can imagine a little widget within the
app alerting the user of the fact, and letting them click through to
explore the result (of course one could set things up such that the
user is emailed upon completion of the app, but still ...).

-steve
